name: Renfield Shake Motor
description:
12V shake motor - 'the signature', Renfield's tremble. BTS7960 / IBT-2 module (sold as HW-039). BCM GPIO: RPWM=12, LPWM=13 (header pins 32 and 33). PROVEN MOVING 2026-09-13 at 30% duty, observed by the operator.

THE TWO THINGS THAT MADE IT WORK, both hardware-only, both of which fail SILENTLY - the wrapper returns success with no motion and nothing in any log says why:
  1. VCC IS A SEPARATE 5V SUPPLY. Unlike the MDD10A this board does not power its logic from the motor rail. VCC -> Pi 5V (header pin 2), GND -> Pi ground (pin 6). Never put 12V on VCC; it destroys the board.
  2. R_EN AND L_EN MUST BE TIED HIGH IN HARDWARE. The software does NOT drive them - setup_bts7960_pins() only writes an enable pin HIGH if renPin/lenPin are configured, and they deliberately are not. Both go to 5V (Pi pin 4 here, same rail as pin 2). Left floating the bridge is disabled and nothing moves.
R_IS and L_IS are current-sense OUTPUTS from the chip, not inputs. Leave them unconnected - jumpering them to VCC can damage it and kills fault detection.

PIN CHOICE: both RPWM and LPWM carry PWM on this board (one at a time, by direction), unlike the MDD10A where DIR was a static level. lgpio.tx_pwm() is SOFTWARE PWM and runs on any GPIO, so nothing today depends on the choice, but 12/13 are the Pi 5's RP1 hardware-PWM pair and would not need rewiring if that ever changes.

12V PATH: B+/B- to the supply, M+/M- to the motor, nothing in line but a slow-blow fuse. No bulk capacitor, no snubber, no series resistor. A fixed resistor can NEVER sit in line with a motor supply - 200 ohm allows 60mA and pins the board near 3.3V; a pre-charge resistor is only valid across a switch that shorts it out.

STILL OUTSTANDING: 10k pull-downs from RPWM and LPWM to ground. With the enables permanently high the bridge is always armed, and a Pi reboot floats both PWM lines - fit them before leaving this unattended.

HISTORY: a Cytron MDD10A was wired here first and destroyed itself with smoke after a couple of minutes powered. Root cause never conclusively established; a reverse-connected bulk electrolytic is the leading candidate. The Pi survived.

Shake is a short burst: scenes run 900-2000ms at 50-80%, maxDuration caps any single energization at 5000ms. A wiper-class motor stalls around 24-40A and cooks until the fuse opens (Groundbreaker, 2026-08-30).
